newCompounds.description: Sharp, cooling compound prominent in rosemary; stimulating in aroma studies.
newCompounds.name: Camphor

newOils.description: Steam-distilled from leaves. High in eucalyptol and camphor; the most researched oil for memory and alertness effects.
newOils.name: Rosemary
newOils.safety: Avoid in pregnancy and with epilepsy; may raise blood pressure.

note: Research batch 2 for ChatGPT to plug into data.js. Every PMID verified against the NCBI E-utilities API (titles and years match). Each study is tagged with plant (oilIds), terpenes (compoundIds), and uses (categories). Merge rule: skip any study whose pubmedId already exists in data.js.

studies.authors: Moss M, Cook J, Wesnes K, Duckett P
studies.finding: Rosemary aroma significantly improved overall memory quality and secondary memory versus controls, while lavender impaired working memory and slowed reaction times on memory and attention tasks.
studies.limitations: Healthy young adults; single brief exposure; laboratory setting.
studies.title: Aromas of rosemary and lavender essential oils differentially affect cognition and mood in healthy adults

studies.authors: Chen PJ, Chou CC, Yang L, Tsai YL, et al.
studies.finding: Lavender aromatherapy massage lowered salivary cortisol and raised IgA immediately after treatment in pregnant women, with higher baseline IgA at 32 and 36 weeks versus study entry.
studies.journal: Journal of Alternative and Complementary Medicine
studies.limitations: n=52; massage confound: aromatherapy massage compared against usual care, not massage alone.
studies.title: Effects of Aromatherapy Massage on Pregnant Women's Stress and Immune Function: A Longitudinal, Prospective, Randomized Controlled Trial

studies.authors: Can Çiçek S, Demir Ş, Yılmaz D, Açıkgöz A, et al.
studies.finding: Lavender aromatherapy by inhalation and foot massage reduced blood pressure, heart rate, serum cortisol, and anxiety in patients with essential hypertension.
studies.limitations: Sample size not verifiable from abstract; single-center trial.
studies.title: The Effect of Aromatherapy on Blood Pressure and Stress Responses by Inhalation and Foot Massage in Patients With Essential Hypertension: Randomized Clinical Trial

studies.authors: Mori HM, Kawanami H, Kawahata H, Aoki M, et al.
studies.finding: Topical lavender oil accelerated wound closure in rats from day 4 to 10, increasing TGF-beta expression, fibroblast numbers, and type I and III collagen.
studies.limitations: Rat model; no human wound-healing data.
studies.title: Wound healing potential of lavender oil by acceleration of granulation and wound contraction through induction of TGF-β in a rat model

studies.authors: Schnitzler P, Schön K, Reichling J
studies.finding: Tea tree oil reduced HSV-1 and HSV-2 plaque formation by 98.2% and 93.0% at noncytotoxic concentrations, acting before or during viral adsorption; eucalyptus oil showed weaker activity.
studies.limitations: In-vitro cell culture only; active antiviral components unidentified.
studies.title: Antiviral activity of Australian tea tree oil and eucalyptus oil against herpes simplex virus in cell culture

studies.authors: Lee JH, Kim YG, Lee J, et al.
studies.finding: Carvacrol-rich oregano oil and thymol-rich thyme oil inhibited uropathogenic E. coli biofilm formation at subinhibitory concentrations and reduced fimbriae, swarming motility, and hemagglutination.
studies.limitations: In-vitro; no human or clinical data.
studies.title: Carvacrol-rich oregano oil and thymol-rich thyme red oil inhibit biofilm formation and the virulence of uropathogenic Escherichia coli

studies.authors: Kumar P, Mishra S, Malik A, Satya S, et al.
studies.finding: Peppermint oil was the most effective housefly repellent of six oils screened, and formulated peppermint and eucalyptus oils cut fly density 96-98% in field trials.
studies.limitations: Laboratory bioassays with limited field validation; not a human-use repellent trial.
studies.title: Repellent, larvicidal and pupicidal properties of essential oils and their formulations against the housefly, Musca domestica

studies.authors: Hur MH, Park J, Maddock-Jennings W, Kim DO, Lee MS
studies.finding: An essential-oil mouthwash (tea tree, peppermint, lemon) reduced oral malodour and volatile sulphur compounds in ICU patients significantly more than benzydamine at one hour.
studies.limitations: n=32; single ICU; follow-up only one hour.
studies.title: Reduction of mouth malodour and volatile sulphur compounds in intensive care patients using an essential oil mouthwash

studies.authors: Ball EL, Owen-Booth B, Gray A, Shenkin SD, et al.
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: across 12 included trials, the Cochrane reviewers found no convincing evidence that aromatherapy benefits people with dementia, with very low certainty throughout.
studies.limitations: Very low certainty evidence; inconsistent outcomes and poor harms reporting across trials.
studies.title: Aromatherapy for dementia

studies.authors: Kuriyama H, Watanabe S, Nakaya T, Shigemori I, et al.
studies.finding: Aromatherapy massage increased peripheral blood lymphocytes, CD8+, and CD16+ cells compared with carrier-oil massage in 11 healthy adults.
studies.limitations: n=11; preliminary; blend also contained cypress and sweet marjoram oils.
studies.title: Immunological and Psychological Benefits of Aromatherapy Massage

studies.authors: Shiina Y, Funabashi N, Lee K, Toyoda T, et al.
studies.finding: Lavender aromatherapy reduced serum cortisol and improved coronary flow velocity reserve in healthy men.
studies.limitations: Small sample; acute effects only; healthy men.
studies.title: Relaxation effects of lavender aromatherapy improve coronary flow velocity reserve in healthy men evaluated by transthoracic Doppler echocardiography

studies.finding: Lavender aromatherapy during dental treatment lowered salivary cortisol, pulse rate, and injection pain scores in children aged 7 to 9.
studies.limitations: n=24 crossover; pediatric dental setting only.
studies.title: The effects of lavender aromatherapy on stress and pain perception in children during dental treatment: A randomized clinical trial

studies.authors: Bikmoradi A, Seifi Z, Poorolajal J, Araghchian M, et al.
studies.finding: NULL RESULT: lavender inhalation aromatherapy had no significant effect on mental stress or vital signs after coronary bypass surgery, except for systolic blood pressure.
studies.limitations: n=60; single center; two-day intervention only.
studies.title: Effect of inhalation aromatherapy with lavender essential oil on stress and vital signs in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass surgery: A single-blinded randomized clinical trial
